skill.name: character-creation-studio
skill.description: Use a Chinese-language workflow to design original characters and casts. Write image prompts, record approved visual traits, and prepare reference sheets for video production.

remediation.issue: Cross-provider image diagnostics do not specify an approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Before switching providers, identify the destination and show what prompts or images would be sent. Ask for approval and offer a local or redacted comparison.

semantic_findings.title: Cross-provider prompt reuse lacks an approval step
semantic_findings.description: The diagnostic workflow suggests rerunning the same prompt on another provider. This can expose unpublished character details if the user has not approved that provider.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly recommends keeping character details when switching models and does not specify a consent check. Actual transfer depends on the available tools.

content.user_title: Design Characters and Prepare Reference Sheets
content.value_statement: A character can look different in each generated image when its defining features are not documented. Record those features once and reuse them in prompts for reference sheets and production handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Expand a one-line brief into a character concept with a distinct silhouette and one to three defining visual traits.
Build a cast matrix that compares silhouettes, palettes, and props while keeping materials and rendering consistent across the group.
Draft GPT Image prompts that separate fixed character traits from the angle, pose, lighting, or expression for a specific image.
Record an approved reference image, feature counts, feature placement, and unresolved details in a character lock record.
Specify turnaround, head, expression, and detail sheets, then check visible traits against the approved reference when images are available.
Prepare a video production handoff checklist with the current reference images, a reusable identity description, and known consistency issues.
limitations: The skill writes prompts and specifications. It requires a separate image tool to generate or edit images.
It cannot guarantee identical character features across generated views. Features that are hidden or unclear remain unverified.
This edition includes sample style descriptions and test results, not the full tables or named creature catalogs.
The workflow prepares character references for video production but does not write video shots or generate video.

use_cases.title: Develop an original character
use_cases.description: Turn a short brief into visible design choices and a prompt for the first reference image.

use_cases.title: Differentiate a game cast
use_cases.description: Compare character silhouettes, proportions, and signature items while using the same materials and rendering style across the cast.

use_cases.title: Hand off approved character references
use_cases.description: Share a current reference set with a reusable identity description, an art review record, and notes on traits that must not change.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first character prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a greenhouse maintenance robot with a tall silhouette. List three defining visual traits and write an English GPT Image prompt. Do not generate images.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Start from a one-line concept.

prompt_templates.title: Make a cast matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three workers for a floating market. Set shared materials and a rendering style. Give each worker a distinct silhouette, color, and signature item.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Plan characters for a shared world.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a three-view sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my approved reference and lock record. Write a prompt for front, side, and back views at equal scale. Keep fixed traits unchanged. Label inferred back details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Prepare a turnaround from an approved character.

prompt_templates.title: Review and prepare a handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my reference sheets with the approved master and lock record. Flag any changed or unverified traits. List only approved assets in the current handoff and include a reusable English identity description.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review an asset set before video production.

output_examples.input: Design a greenhouse maintenance robot. Provide a concept and a master image prompt only.
output: Design: A tall robot with a narrow, moss-green body, a single amber lens, and a brass sprayer on its left hip.
Master image prompt: Show the full robot from the front with soft, even lighting and a plain light gray background. Keep the lens and sprayer visible.
Status: Prompt ready. No image generated.

output_examples.input: Review the supplied turnaround against the approved robot reference and lock record.
output: Pass: All three views show the same body proportions and moss-green panels.
Fail: The rear view moves the brass sprayer to the robot's right hip. The lock record places it on the left.
Decision: Hold the turnaround for revision. The amber lens is not visible from the back and remains unverified in that view.

best_practices: Approve one reference image before recording fixed traits and generating alternate views.
Assign each reference image a specific purpose, such as identity, costume, or rendering style.
Compare generated images with the approved reference and count visible details before marking them as verified.
anti_patterns: Changing the face, outfit, and pose in the same edit.
Using a portrait with heavy shadows as the only reference for facial structure.
Treating a written prompt check or a hidden feature as proof of image consistency.

faq.question: Can I use this skill without an image tool?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft concepts, prompts, and asset specifications. It cannot generate images or verify visual consistency without seeing the results.

faq.question: Does the lock record guarantee matching images?
faq.answer: No. It records what must stay fixed and gives you a checklist for review. Image models can still change those traits.

faq.question: Can I start with an existing illustration?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell the skill which traits to keep and which to change. It can record visible details and label assumptions about obscured areas.

faq.question: Which image tools does the workflow cover?
faq.answer: GPT Image is the main workflow. The references also describe style exploration in Midjourney and still-image style tests in Grok Imagine.

faq.question: Does this include every style description and test result?
faq.answer: No. This edition includes 20 complete style entries, an index of the remaining entries, and sample results for Midjourney and Grok Imagine.

faq.question: What goes into the video handoff?
faq.answer: The standard set includes the approved master, turnaround, head views, expressions, details, and a portrait. It also includes the lock record and a reusable identity description.
